title: Trying out new scores on the Cotton Club floor
summary: Duke handed him a score to copy by morning, then he would play a chorus on piano and the band would try it at first sight while the dancers carried on.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: So how long had you been working with Duke when you started writing again?

Oh, pretty near as soon as I joined the band almost. He started giving me something to do, right away, you know? I guess he was trying to find out what I could do, you know; if I could do the extraction, because he used to give it to me, like, today, and tonight when I get through, he'd hand me a little score or something, and I'd go home where we used to live and write until about eight or nine o'clock, and bring it in that afternoon or that night to the Cotton Club, and we'd try it out at first sight.

And the way we would try it out, he would play one chorus by himself on the piano, and then the next chord, chorus, we'd go with the band, and we'd start the band, and it'd be the same chord. If we didn't do it right, then he'd play another chorus on the piano, and we tried it with the band until we got the whole tune together.
Oh, certainly. Certainly. He wanted to hear the band, and to avoid that, while the people were still

dancing -- they didn't know the difference -- because he was playing on the piano the same music, he was playing the chorus of his own music, and we were working and starting the same tune over there with the whole band until we got it together.
He often did that on the job?
Oh, yes, right on the job he would do a lot of things first sight.
When you first started extracting for him, did you immediately understand what he wanted? I mean did you know what he meant by the way he wrote it down?

Oh, sure, because like I say, it was all for four trombones, four saxaphones, three trumpets and two trombones -- we used the saxaphone when he was in concert; I transposed for this part for the saxaphones, and then for the trumpets in B flat. He was in concert, and I would transpose the trumpet; the only one that he wouldn't have to transpose was the trombones.
The whole concert -- trombones, they would play in concerts, you know?
